Status:
- Open the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx and go to the Operating sheet. Plant 7799, generator 34, reads 'Status (OP) Operating', nameplate 83.0 MW, operating June 2000, owner Madison Gas & Electric Co. The planned retirement columns are blank.
- Open the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources air permit 43802242A-P40, issued June 15, 2026, at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1275530. Section A lists 'Stack S04; Process P04 - 102 MW simple cycle combustion turbine generator (unit M34)'. A new five-year permit was issued, so the owner plans to keep running it.
- I found no retirement, mothballing or owner change. The 102 MW in the permit is a permit rating, so the 83.0 MW nameplate stays.

Backup Power.note:
Backup Power:
- No document uses the words 'backup power' for this unit, so the value of no is inferred.
- Open the air permit at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1275530. Process P04 is a simple cycle combustion turbine at an 'electric generation facility' that tracks hours 'in peak power mode'. It is a grid peaking unit, not a standby set for a single site.
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists the sector as Electric Utility. No data center or site load is named. So the value stays no.
